transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. Thank you for coming in today. What brings you to the clinic?

Yeah, hi. Um... I guess I'm just having a hard time sitting still. 

Like, whenever I have to stay put in the radiology suite or in class, I just... I don't know, I feel like I'm crawling out of my skin. I've been trying to just tough it out for months, but... I always end up pacing, or shifting around, or just finding some excuse to get up and move. So... yeah. That's why I'm here.
When did you first notice this difficulty sitting still? Has this been something you've dealt with since childhood, or is this more recent?

Um... no, it's not recent. It's been a long time. Since childhood, I guess. 

My parents still talk about it sometimes. Like, these elementary school conferences where... the teachers would complain. They said I was always getting out of my seat, or... calling out, rushing ahead before they even finished giving directions. 

So... yeah. It was happening way before middle school. Not just since I started the radiology training.
When you're sitting still, do you find it hard to concentrate or keep your mind on one thing, or is it more that you just feel physically uncomfortable and need to move?
Um... I don't know. I guess... it's just the physical part. I just feel like I have to move. I haven't really noticed the other stuff.
When you're working on something or reading, do you find yourself getting distracted easily, or do you have trouble keeping your attention on tasks even when you're sitting still?
Um... no, not really. I mean, I can read fine. It's just... I just don't like sitting there doing it. My mind doesn't really wander, I just... I just want to get up.
Do you find yourself making careless mistakes in your work or studies, or do you often forget things you're supposed to remember?
Um... no. Not really. I don't think I make mistakes like that. I usually remember what I'm supposed to do.
Do you find yourself doing things without thinking first, or acting on impulse? For example, interrupting people, blurting things out, or making quick decisions you later regret?

Um... yeah, I guess. Sometimes. Like... if my supervisor is explaining a positioning step or asking a question, I'll just kind of... jump in with the answer before they finish. And then... I realize I missed the part that actually mattered. So... yeah.

When you're not in situations where you have to sit still, like when you're at home or somewhere you can move around freely, do you still feel like you have excess energy or a need to be doing something physical? Or does that restless feeling mainly happen when you're forced to stay in one place?

Um... no, it's pretty much everywhere. I don't really stop. Like... most days I just go from class straight to clinicals, then the gym, errands... I just keep moving. 

If there's a gap in my schedule, I... I just immediately find something else to do. Sitting around, even at home, is just... it feels almost impossible. So I just keep doing stuff.

How much has this difficulty sitting still and constant need to move affected your ability to do well in your radiology training, or caused problems in other areas of your life like relationships or your health?

Um... yeah, it's... it's caused some problems. In my training, mostly. 

My... my clinical evaluations haven't been great lately. They actually... they put me on a formal remediation plan. The supervisors said I was disrupting patient flow and... making teamwork harder, I guess. 

It's just... I'm really worried about it. If I can't figure out how to fix it, I might... I might lose my spot in the program.

When you're doing something that really interests you or that you find engaging—like a procedure you enjoy or a hobby—can you focus on that for a long time without getting distracted, or do you still struggle to keep your attention on it?

Um... I'm not really sure. I haven't... I haven't really paid attention to that. I guess I just... do whatever I'm supposed to be doing. I haven't really thought about whether it's different for stuff I actually like. So... yeah, I don't know.

When you're doing your radiology training—looking at images or reviewing cases—do you find yourself missing important details or having to go back and re-check things because you didn't catch something the first time?

Um... I don't really know. I mean, everyone misses things sometimes, right? I just... I do my work. I haven't really noticed if I have to go back more than anyone else. I just try to get through the cases.

Do you find yourself frequently losing important things like your keys, phone, or paperwork? Or do you have trouble keeping track of tasks and deadlines without writing them down or setting reminders?
Um... I guess I lose stuff sometimes. Just normal things, like anyone. I don't really know if it's frequent. I just... I get my work done. I haven't really thought about it.

When you're in class or during clinical training and the supervisor is explaining something important, do you find yourself having trouble following along or remembering what they said, even when you're trying hard to pay attention?
Uh... I don't know. I mean, I just listen to what they're saying. I don't really keep track of how much I remember later on. I just... try to do what they asked. It seems fine, I guess.

When you're working on radiology cases or studying for exams, do you ever have trouble organizing your thoughts or materials, or do you find yourself starting tasks but then moving on to something else before finishing them?
Uh... not really. I don't really pay attention to how my stuff is organized. I just... do the assignments. I haven't noticed leaving things unfinished or anything. I just study like normal, I guess.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient presents with lifelong history of hyperactivity-impulsivity symptoms since elementary school, including persistent difficulty sitting still, constant need for movement, excessive energy, and impulsive behavior (interrupting others, jumping to conclusions). Minimal inattention symptoms reported. Clear functional impairment documented in radiology training program (formal remediation plan, disrupted patient flow, teamwork difficulties). Symptoms present across multiple settings (class, clinicals, home) and do not appear situational. While some inattention features cannot be entirely ruled out, the clinical presentation is predominantly hyperactive-impulsive type ADHD.
